Arrive Singapore Changi — connection to.closedNote: Almost every airside item at Changi is open 24 hours, so HOURS ARE NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT — terminal and airside-versus-landside are. Open through the 12:05-13:20 window and verified from Changi's own pages: Dreamscape, Enchanted Garden, Sunflower Garden, Fit&Fun Zone, Calm Room, the T1/T2/T3 prayer rooms, all six free snooze lounges, every transit smoking area, T3 Butterfly Garden, T3 Crystal Garden, T3 Movie Theatre, T1 Cactus/Discovery/Water Lily gardens, airside baggage storage and the Ambassador transit lounges and hotels. The hours block above is the Skytrain's 05:00-02:00 window expressed per day, since that is the only published time that actually gates movement. LANDSIDE TRAPS, all confirmed from Changi's own attraction pages, which tag each item Public or Transit. UNREACHABLE in transit: Jewel entirely (Rain Vortex, Shiseido Forest Valley, Canopy Park, YOTELAIR, Changi Lounge) — "you will need to clear arrival immigration"; The Wonderfall (T2 Public L2, easily confused with Dreamscape, which IS airside); Flap Pix (T2 Public L3); Kinetic Rain (T1 Public L2); Arrival Garden (T1 Public); ST3PS free-movie space (T3 basement, Public); and the S$5 Hub & Spoke showers (T2 Public L1). ALL FOUR VIEWING MALLS ARE PUBLIC, and T2's is additionally "temporary closed from 19 June to 30 September 2026" — inside both trip dates — so airside plane-spotting is Gourmet Garden's windows ("16 different tailfins") or the Sunflower Garden deck, not a viewing mall. The Free Singapore Tour needs a layover of "at least 5.5 hours" and is ineligible in both windows, though its booths are useful airside landmarks: T2 L2 near Gate F50 and T3 L2 near Gates A1-A8, both 08:00-19:00. Swee Choon, Curry Times, PappaRich, Peach Garden, Paradise Dynasty and Ya Kun Family Cafe (T3) are all Public-only despite appearing in a 2023 factsheet's transit list. There is no admission charge for any transit area. One structural caveat on F&B: Changi's dining directory and its per-outlet pages are JavaScript-driven and return no hours or prices, so NO airside restaurant's opening hours and NO food price could be sourced. What is solid is outlet name plus terminal plus level plus transit-or-public, from Changi's own Changi Pay outlet list. Halal is verified in writing for only three: Encik Tan ("Halal-certified mini food atrium", per its operator Fei Siong), IRVINS (marked per product) and Old Chang Kee (brand-published claim, certifying body not stated). Everything else — The Satay Club, Ya Kun, Wee Nam Kee, The Hainan Story, every Straits Food Street stall — is UNVERIFIED, and MUIS's own certification directory was unreachable. Do not tell 35 people something is halal on the strength of a category.

Japan (with the exception of SQ12) and South Korea should check in at Terminal 2" — so SQ634 and SQ142 depart T2 on the operator's own rule, which upgrades the flight-tracker guess. subRoutes.title: Two levels, seventy-five minutes: the T2 airside loop

steps.name: Dreamscape, Level 2 — catch one show cycle
steps.note: First because it is the only thing with a clock: the light-and-sound cycle runs every 15 minutes, so arriving early costs nothing and arriving late costs the frame.

steps.name: Gourmet Garden, same level — eat
steps.note: Multi-stall, so 35 people split across counters and re-form at tables. Encik Tan is the halal-in-writing alternative if anyone needs certainty rather than a category.

steps.name: Up to Level 3 — prayer room, opposite Lift Lobby 21
steps.note: One climb serves the rest of this route. Ablution facilities and qibla signage are published; capacity is not, so rotate.

steps.name: Sunflower Garden, same Level 3 — outdoors
steps.note: Runs alongside the prayer rotation rather than after it: whoever is waiting goes out on the roof deck. No seat count, so all 35 fit.

steps.name: Down to the pier and the gate
steps.note: The snooze lounges sit opposite E5, E11 and F33 — i.e. at the boarding piers — so heading for them is the same direction as heading for the gate.

subRoutes.note: Deliberately confined to T2 and to two levels, because that is what the published record can actually support: Changi gives no Skytrain journey time, so a T2-to-T3 Butterfly Garden round trip cannot be sized on a 2h10 connection. Level 2 has Dreamscape, the food and the snooze lounges; Level 3 has the prayer room and the roof. Deadline 13:20 walking to the gate, because Changi screens at the holdroom and 35 people are one queue. If the flight lands at T3 instead, drop this and use Butterfly Garden and the free Movie Theatre, both airside there.

Kueh lapis and pineapple tarts are fresh bakery and will not survive it; bak kwa is pork and a meat product facing Japanese import rules tonight. The outbound answer is: note the shops, walk past them.
